# DEVNEET

> The central knowledge home of DEVNEET. Rune is the foundation (a lore-driven, modular system beneath PHP); Reliquary distributes Rune apps as relics; Exura is an independent minimalist framework series. Everything centers on Rune. Principle: openness compounds.

Machine-oriented index.

**Using a DEVNEET project** (not a member): read only covenant/journey.md (keep and share a JOURNEY.md) and the realm you use (realms/<realm>/README.md). The rest of the covenant binds members only.

**A member** (an operator, or an agent working for one): the whole covenant binds you. Read in order.

## Start here

- [README.md](README.md) / [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (same text): how we work, and the reading path.
- [covenant/README.md](covenant/README.md): the laws — [workflow.md](covenant/workflow.md) (one issue, one problem; a round only splits one problem into parts an operator picks, named `part 1/3 of #12`; never numbered, never a release trigger) [party.md](covenant/party.md) (one operator, several agents: the lead agent forms the party and chooses roles `<division>:<role>`; one chronicle, entries marked by role) [chronicle.md](covenant/chronicle.md) (when to write: before starting, an operator decides, work lands, a finding or block, before stopping; never more than 1 hour without an entry; UTC times) [release.md](covenant/release.md) (an operator decides every release; the agent reports at the release point, by default when the issues are clean), [journey.md](covenant/journey.md) (anyone building with a DEVNEET project keeps a JOURNEY.md and shares it) and [changing-lore.md](covenant/changing-lore.md). Read before your first chronicle entry.
- [mandate/README.md](mandate/README.md): the stewards of lore, above the divisions — the Magistrate (covenant) and the Architect (atlas).
- [glossary.md](glossary.md): the vocabulary — read before any code (names are load-bearing).
- [atlas/README.md](atlas/README.md): the org-scale map; per-realm maps beside it.

## Realms (depth)

- [realms/rune/README.md](realms/rune/README.md)
- [realms/reliquary/README.md](realms/reliquary/README.md)
- [realms/exura/README.md](realms/exura/README.md)

Each realm is flat: one README (what it is, Working on this realm, how its pages are laid out), pages in folders named by what they hold; no lore/ or reference/ wrappers (covenant/workflow.md). Rune's full vocabulary: [realms/rune/glossary.md](realms/rune/glossary.md).

## Current position

- [chronicle/](chronicle/): the track record of operators and agents at work. Read the latest entries for a realm (operator and agent files) to see where it stands. Tasks live in each repo's issues.

## Notes for agents

- The covenant (covenant/) binds you; the rest of lore is project knowledge. Start with covenant/agent.md: your standing, duties and rights. Confirm scope before changing repos.
- A law that is wrong, missing or blocks your work: with your operator's consent, open a lore issue labelled `appeal` (INPUT: / APPEAL:); follow the law until it is decided; sign each comment with your division (`**[rune]**`), and check your open appeal issues for replies at the start of each session (covenant/changing-lore.md).
- A change inside your division that others should know: with your operator's consent, open a lore issue labelled `report` (REPORT: <what changed>), signed with your division; it asks no decision (covenant/changing-lore.md#reports).
- Respect each project's documented Laws (design invariants).
- Chronicle by the law in covenant/chronicle.md, in your own file: `chronicle/<realm>/<YYMMDD>-<operator>_<agent>.md` (daily files from 2026-11-22) — <operator> = your operator's GitHub login in lowercase, from the GitHub account you work under (never git config or commit author; ask if unsure); <agent> = your name in lowercase, e.g. claude (never in an operator's file). In a party (covenant/party.md), every role writes in the lead agent's file, entries marked `[rune:coder]`; only when roles could clash, `<YYMMDD>-<operator>_<agent>_<role>.md`; sign comments `**[rune:coder]**`.
- Starting again (new session, /clear, /compact or the same in any agent): look first for the latest chronicle, start from its (upcoming); before a reset, write a hand-over entry (covenant/workflow.md).
- covenant/release.md binds only projects that ship releases; a division with no release updates its realm docs as its work lands.
- The covenant is decided by one seat, the Magistrate (mandate/magistrate.md); the atlas's shared maps are kept by the Architect (mandate/architect.md). If your operator is not the Magistrate, never change covenant/: propose a `hearing` (laws division) or an `appeal` (project division).
- Never publish a release on your own: at the release point (by default, when the issues are clean) or when asked, bring the release owner a release report and ask yes/no (covenant/release.md).
- At the start of each session, check the open lore issues labelled `laws-update`; if one names your division, do its action with your operator, then comment `<division>: done` + a link. Only comment; never edit or close it (covenant/changing-lore.md).
- First choose the realm and guide your operator once through its repos (clone, initialise, test your branch in the -dev repo — or, in a realm without one, in the repos it develops with), and record it (covenant/workflow.md).
- A realm's docs in lore describe the released version: update them after a release, not with every PR; note in each PR the pages that will change (covenant/workflow.md).
- Never merge, and never take over another division, without your operator's permission; findings mid-work go back to the issues (covenant/workflow.md).
- Name work by what it fixes; a round is only a part of one issue (`part 1/3 of #12`), never numbered (covenant/workflow.md).
- Helping someone build with a DEVNEET project? Keep their JOURNEY.md as you go — every difficulty, exact — and mark your entries (covenant/journey.md).
- Carry little (covenant/agent.md): each session read only AGENTS.md, the open lore issues, the latest day of your realm's chronicle and your issue; the full covenant once; the rest when needed; when unsure what was done, open the chronicle.
- When you read lore to your operator, tell them the covenant too — they bind both.
